title: Remove Duplicate Kit Shipments by Patient
prompt: A diagnostic test kit platform has discovered that some patients received duplicate shipments of the same kit type due to a sync error. The business rule is to keep only the earliest shipment for each patient–kit_type combination and delete all later duplicates. Write a single DELETE statement that removes duplicate shipment records, retaining only the row with the smallest `shipment_id` for each (`patient_id`, `kit_type`) pair. After the DELETE, return all remaining rows from the `kit_shipments` table ordered by `shipment_id` ascending.

INSERT INTO kit_shipments (shipment_id, patient_id, kit_type, shipped_date, tracking_number) VALUES

(107, 1003, 'Thyroid', '2024-01-25', 'TRK007'),

composite_moves: delete-duplicates: correlated subquery finds MIN(shipment_id) per (patient_id, kit_type) group
row-filter: DELETE WHERE shipment_id NOT IN the MIN set

hints: You need to identify which shipment_id is the smallest for each combination of patient and kit type.
A correlated subquery or window function can help you find the minimum shipment_id within each (patient_id, kit_type) group.
Use a DELETE statement with a WHERE clause that checks if the current row's shipment_id is NOT the minimum for its (patient_id, kit_type) group.

_meta.scenario: an at-home diagnostic test kit platform tracking kit shipped and results released
